incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: alert fired for service=inference-routing (high error rate) — PD-INC-7841. Auto-escalation in 3m if unacked. https://pagerduty.example/PD-INC-7841
jamie (oncall): Acked the page, jumping in. Seeing 5xxs in logs, looks like kv-cache saturating on gpu-pool-a.
priya (sre): thanks — can you paste the first error stack or curl output?
jamie (oncall): quick log snippet:
```
ERROR 2026-03-14T20:12:31Z inference-routing: kv_cache_evictions=1200 latency_ms=450 status=503 model=redwood-v1
stack: grpc: code = ResourceExhausted
```

sara (eng): holding — we're also seeing a second PD alert for the same window: PD-INC-7842 (embeddings-queue high latency). They might be related (shared GPU pool).
evan (cs): multiple customers are reporting timeouts on embeddings API, one active enterprise customer (Acme) is seeing 504s. Marking P1-customer-impact.
priya (sre): oncall note: both PD incidents routed to different rotations and got auto-escalated, so ownership is sticky in both incidents. We need a single primary owner to coordinate. @jamie can you be primary for inference-routing and @matt take embeddings-queue?
jamie (oncall): I can be primary for inference-routing. I'll try a quick remediation: increase pool size for gpu-pool-a by 2 nodes. Running scale command now:
```
redwoodctl pool scale --name=gpu-pool-a --delta=2 --reason="eviction spike"
```
matt (platform): I'm taking embeddings-queue primary. Thx. I see autoscaler is at 80% and throttling back because of spot pressure. I'll trigger a temporary override to allow burst nodes.
sara (eng): note — there are duplicated PD alerts for the same underlying fault. suggest a follow-up to merge alerts or update routing rules so we don't split ownership next time.
priya (sre): pragmatic steps: 1) scale up gpu-pool-a (jamie) 2) temporarily disable spot-only policy for burst (matt) 3) enable prefix cache warm for embeddings workload (sara). Also toggling alert thresholds to reduce dup pages.
jamie (oncall): scale command returned success, nodes provisioning: 2 -> provisioning. Watching logs.
incident-bot: PD-INC-7841 acknowledged by jamie (oncall). PD-INC-7842 acknowledged by matt (platform).
evan (cs): Acme restarted their job and is seeing fewer errors now — they reported a 60% drop in failures.
matt (platform): override applied to autoscaler for 20m (allow-burst=true). New nodes starting.
jamie (oncall): logs after scale:
```
INFO 2026-03-14T20:17:40Z inference-routing: kv_cache_evictions=200 latency_ms=120 status=200
```

priya (sre): metrics look good — error rate back to baseline. Can we keep pages open for 15m to watch for regressions?
sara (eng): warm cache hook applied to embeddings route. running synthetic requests to rehydrate KV prefixes.
evan (cs): telling Acme we're monitoring and will update in 15. they appreciate the quick turnaround.
jamie (oncall): holding primary. if stable in 15m I'll close PD-INC-7841 and post a short incident note.
matt (platform): same for PD-INC-7842.
priya (sre): postmortem action items: - adjust alert routing to reduce duplicate PD incidents - add autoscaler fallback when spot pressure high - add a runbook section about 'concurrent pages, single ownership' - investigate kv-cache eviction root cause (possible memory leak)
evan (cs): noted — will coordinate customer update after close.
incident-bot: PD-INC-7841 marked resolved (closed by jamie). PD-INC-7842 marked resolved (closed by matt).
jamie (oncall): thanks everyone. short blameless recap: concurrent pages caused split acknowledgment and delayed unified mitigation. mitigations worked (scale + autoscaler override + cache warm). follow-ups as priy listed. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
